author: TEDx Talks
description:
Former senior U.S. national security official Miles Taylor shares a personal account that raises a broader civic concern: the growing cost of dissent in American public life. Drawing on his experience inside government and the consequences of speaking openly, Taylor explores how fear, intimidation, and self-censorship are affecting people across the political spectrum — from public servants to private citizens.

Taylor's account highlights the risks to democracies when dissent is no longer acceptable, and the foundational role of free expression in a democratic society. He underscores the difference between criticism and disloyalty, and why a healthy democracy depends on citizens who are willing to speak openly — even when it feels uncomfortable or risky. Miles Taylor is a national security expert, New York Times best-selling author, and renowned technologist. title: The rising cost of dissent in America | Miles Taylor | TEDxMidAtlantic

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Olympic gold medalist Connor Fields asks one powerful question: When life says, “Now what?” how do you respond?

After a life-threatening crash at the Tokyo Olympic Games left him with broken ribs, a collapsed lung, and bleeding on four different parts of his brain, Connor woke up alone in a hospital bed, unsure if he would fully recover. Just days earlier, he had entered the Games as the top-ranked rider, chasing another medal.

In this gripping TEDxLasVegas talk, the three-time Olympian shares the three races that altered the course of his life: falling short in the 2012 Olympic final, becoming the first American to win Olympic BMX gold at the 2016 Rio Games, and surviving a devastating crash at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics that led to a traumatic brain injury and more than a year of rehabilitation.

What connects those moments is not just talent or training, but the choices he made in between.

title: Now what? The question that follows triumph and tragedy | Connor Fields | TEDxLasVegas

In divided times, how do you advance equity without deepening division? And what happens to organizations when they get it right, or dangerously wrong?

Across industries, inclusion efforts are being questioned, scaled back, or quietly removed. Some say these programs hurt performance. Others insist they are essential to fairness and long-term success. But what if the real issue is not whether equity matters, but how it is pursued?

In this thoughtful and strategic talk, Gwen Migita shares a deeply personal story that reshaped how she approaches opposition, persuasion, and progress. Drawing on leadership experience across sectors, she challenges the assumption that advancing fairness requires fighting harder.

She also makes a compelling business case: when approached thoughtfully, inclusion is not a liability. It can strengthen organizations, build trust and loyalty, reduce risk, and unlock long-term growth.

This is not a talk about shouting louder. It is about influence, strategy,
title: The power of equity done right | Gwen Migita | TEDxLasVegas

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In too many communities, it is easier to buy liquor than fresh produce. Easier to find processed snacks than fresh meat or vegetables. This is the reality of food deserts, neighborhoods where access to affordable, nutritious food is limited or nonexistent. But food insecurity is not just about supply. It is about dignity.

Pastor and community leader DeWayne McCoy explores how the shift from community-centered markets to profit-driven grocery chains reshaped entire neighborhoods. When local stores disappeared, so did access, accountability, and compassion. What replaced them were systems built to maximize revenue, not restore resilience.

But this is not a talk that ends with frustration. It is a blueprint for what is possible.

With more than two decades of experience in grocery operations, logistics, and hunger relief, McCoy shares a proven hybrid model that combines sustainable retail with a free food pantry. A business designed not only to generate revenue, but to strengthen the v
title: Restoring dignity to food deserts | DeWayne McCoy | TEDxLasVegas

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Why do people resist even the best advice and why do most attempts to influence fail in the long run?
In this thought-provoking talk, the speaker explores the true role of a leader: not to convince, persuade, or manipulate but to influence authentically. Drawing from everyday human behavior, the talk highlights a fundamental truth: if we struggle to follow our own intentions, no amount of pressure or logic will make others change either.
The speaker challenges the conventional idea of influence as selling, persuading, or pushing ideas. Instead, they introduce authentic influence—the ability to create powerful mental shifts that help people move faster toward their own goals, without resistance. When influence is authentic, people don’t feel sold to; they feel supported.
The talk outlines three key principles of authentic influence:
Leading with intention to serve rather than sell
Going beyond logic to address subconscious programming that drives behavior

In a world obsessed with the big picture, we often overlook the details that give places their true meaning. In this talk, Architect Wisam Allami explores how hidden beauty reveals itself when we slow down, observe carefully, and learn to listen to our surroundings.

Drawing from architecture, photography, and personal experience, he challenges the idea that beauty must be created from scratch. Instead, he argues that it already exists, in materials, textures, history, and everyday moments, waiting to be noticed. By changing how we see, we can transform not only the spaces we design, but the way we experience the world around us. Wisam Allami is an architect and founder of LAMI Architects, based in Dubai, working across residential, cultural, and hospitality projects in the Middle East, India, Turkey, and beyond. His work centers on creating meaningful connections between people, place, and nature, with human experience at the core.

description: Every human life begins with a code of three billion letters of DNA that shape who we are. But what happens when just one letter changes? For millions living with rare genetic disorders, that single alteration can mean years of uncertainty, misdiagnosis, and unanswered questions. In this talk, Dr. Murtadha Ali, a senior clinical genomics scientist, takes us on a journey from bacterial genomes to the human genome, revealing how cutting-edge sequencing technologies are ending diagnostic odysseys for families worldwide. Through real-life cases, he shows how whole-genome sequencing uncovers hidden mutations, transforms medical care, and restores hope. Dr. Murtadha Ali is a senior clinical genomics scientist with more than a decade of expertise in molecular diagnostics and rare genetic disorders.
